claims.explanation: Bergenin's anti-inflammatory activity via NF-κB inhibition and PPARγ agonism may sensitize cancer cells that depend on NF-κB signaling for survival, while cells with intact antioxidant pathways (e.g., NFE2L2/KEAP1 mutations) or low NF-κB activity are protected. The selective killing pattern suggests that mutations in KEAP1/NFE2L2 and high expression of NF-κB target genes or PPARγ could predict sensitivity.

features.basis: NFE2L2 mutations activate antioxidant response, potentially counteracting bergenin's pro-oxidant effects; observed in least affected line HEC265.
KEAP1 mutations activate NRF2, enhancing antioxidant capacity; observed in least affected line HEC265.
Bergenin acts as PPARγ agonist; high expression may enhance sensitivity.
Bergenin inhibits NF-κB; high NF-κB activity may confer dependence and sensitivity.
Bergenin inhibits TNF production; high TNF expression may indicate inflammatory dependence.
Bergenin inhibits IL-1β; high expression may indicate inflammatory dependence.
TP53 mutations are common in selectively killed lines, possibly due to loss of antioxidant defense.
EGFR mutations observed in multiple sensitive lung lines; may link to NF-κB activation.
BRAF mutations observed in sensitive melanoma lines; may link to inflammatory signaling.
PTEN mutations observed in sensitive lines; may enhance NF-κB activity.
KRAS mutations observed in sensitive lines; may link to inflammatory pathways.
CDKN2A mutations observed in least affected lines; may indicate reduced sensitivity.
